intent: My brother uses $30 earbuds and swears they sound the same as my friend's $280 pair, and honestly on the bus I couldn't tell them apart either. Before I upgrade mine I want to know where the money actually stops buying sound in true wireless earbuds. Is there a real cutoff price, and does stuff like aptX or other fancy Bluetooth codecs shift it, or is that only audible on gear I'll never own? Owners of both cheap and flagship buds must have opinions here. Tell me the price you'd stop at and the pair to get there.
author_notes: Deep-tier task v1 — see configs/deep_topics/V1_TASK_DESIGN_GRID.md §2 for spec.
intent_v1_legacy: We're six weeks from our due date and the baby-gear marketing is starting to scare me. Wedge pillows that 'reduce SIDS', formulas 'closest to breast milk', car seats you keep rear-facing past age two, sleep sacks being safer than swaddles after eight weeks, anti-colic bottles that supposedly cut crying. Which of these are actually true and which are preying on nervous first-time parents like us? I'd especially like to know where the real pediatric guidance from groups like the AAP lands on each one, and a short safe-sleep list I can tape to the nursery wall.

tri_source.angle: True wireless earbuds price ladder: where the $30-to-$300 diminishing-returns cutoff sits and whether fancy codecs move it
